      "title": "Incorrect organizer UTC offset calculation uses Date.toString()",
      "body": "`dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` first converts the Date to a string in the environment's local timezone, then interprets that string as if it were in `override.timeZone`. This changes the instant. For example, if the server runs in UTC, a Date representing 14:00 IST would be converted to an 08:30 UTC string, and then parsed as 08:30 IST, completely shifting the time. The correct approach is `dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. This bug causes date override windows to be placed at wrong times for all users when the server timezone differs from the organizer's timezone."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/slots.ts",

      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Date override start/end minutes are computed in UTC instead of invitee timezone",
      "body": "The code computes `startTime` and `endTime` as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, \"minute\").hour() * 60 + ...`. This keeps the time in UTC (after shifting by offset) and extracts hour/minute without converting to the invitee's timezone. The resulting minutes are relative to UTC midnight, not to the invitee's local midnight, which is what `buildSlots` expects. This produces incorrect slot times whenever the invitee timezone is not UTC. The correct implementation is to use `dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).hour()*60 + dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).minute()` (and similarly for end). This bug affects all events with date overrides and a non-UTC invitee timezone."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 117,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Date override logic marks partially overlapping slots as available",
      "body": "In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date override check only rejects slots that are entirely before the override start or entirely after the override end (by checking `slotEndTime.isBefore(start)` / `slotEndTime.isSame(start)` and `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)`). A slot that starts before the override start but ends inside the override window will not be rejected and will be considered available. Since a date override replaces normal working hours, any slot not fully contained in the override should be unavailable. This can lead to bookings being offered that begin before the host's available time."
    },

      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 141,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Working hours check uses slot start for both start and end and ignores timezone",
      "body": "In the working-hours validation added to `checkIfIsAvailable`, `const start` and `const end` are both set to `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. This means the check never accounts for the event length, and also uses the slot's UTC time directly without converting to the organizer's timezone. Working hours are defined in the organizer's local time. As a result, valid slots may be rejected or invalid slots allowed for any non-UTC timezone. The check should compare the slot's start and end times (in the organizer's timezone) against the working hour boundaries."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 107,
      "severity": "high",

This computes the wrong offset and causes the subsequent day comparison (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, \"minutes\").format(\"YYYY MM DD\")`) to potentially match the wrong day. The correct approach is to directly format `date.start` in the organizer's timezone using `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone).format(\"YYYY MM DD\")` without any manual offset manipulation."

There is no test covering the round-robin scenario where a fixed host has a date override and a non-fixed host is available. Without such a test, the core bug fix is unverified and could regress silently."

findings.title: Incorrect organizer UTC offset calculation uses Date.toString()
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` first converts the Date to a string in the environment's local timezone, then interprets that string as if it were in `override.timeZone`. This changes the instant. For example, if the server runs in UTC, a Date representing 14:00 IST would be converted to an 08:30 UTC string, and then parsed as 08:30 IST, completely shifting the time. The correct approach is `dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. This bug causes date override windows to be placed at wrong times for all users when the server timezone differs from the organizer's timezone.

findings.title: Date override start/end minutes are computed in UTC instead of invitee timezone
findings.body: The code computes `startTime` and `endTime` as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...`. This keeps the time in UTC (after shifting by offset) and extracts hour/minute without converting to the invitee's timezone. The resulting minutes are relative to UTC midnight, not to the invitee's local midnight, which is what `buildSlots` expects. This produces incorrect slot times whenever the invitee timezone is not UTC. The correct implementation is to use `dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).hour()*60 + dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).minute()` (and similarly for end). This bug affects all events with date overrides and a non-UTC invitee timezone.

findings.title: Date override logic marks partially overlapping slots as available
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date override check only rejects slots that are entirely before the override start or entirely after the override end (by checking `slotEndTime.isBefore(start)` / `slotEndTime.isSame(start)` and `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)`). A slot that starts before the override start but ends inside the override window will not be rejected and will be considered available. Since a date override replaces normal working hours, any slot not fully contained in the override should be unavailable. This can lead to bookings being offered that begin before the host's available time.

findings.title: Working hours check uses slot start for both start and end and ignores timezone
findings.body: In the working-hours validation added to `checkIfIsAvailable`, `const start` and `const end` are both set to `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. This means the check never accounts for the event length, and also uses the slot's UTC time directly without converting to the organizer's timezone. Working hours are defined in the organizer's local time. As a result, valid slots may be rejected or invalid slots allowed for any non-UTC timezone. The check should compare the slot's start and end times (in the organizer's timezone) against the working hour boundaries.

findings.title: UTC offset for date override is computed incorrectly
findings.body: `const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0;` treats `date.start` (an absolute Date object) as if it were a local time string in `organizerTimeZone`. This computes the wrong offset and causes the subsequent day comparison (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")`) to potentially match the wrong day. The correct approach is to directly format `date.start` in the organizer's timezone using `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY MM DD")` without any manual offset manipulation.

findings.title: Missing test for round-robin fixed host date overrides
findings.body: The PR description states it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the only added test is for a personal event with a different attendee timezone. There is no test covering the round-robin scenario where a fixed host has a date override and a non-fixed host is available. Without such a test, the core bug fix is unverified and could regress silently.
